Chapter 6: Innovation Accounting—Tracking Real Progress
Now that you’ve built some momentum with experimentation and decision-making, let’s talk about something just as important—measuring real progress. Because, let’s face it, it’s easy to keep busy, but how do you know if you’re actually moving forward?
That’s where innovation accounting comes in. Think of it as a set of signposts guiding you down a foggy, unfamiliar road. When you’re not sure exactly where you’re headed, these markers help you and your team figure out if you’re on the right track.
The whole process unfolds in three main stages.
First, you need to establish a baseline. This means measuring how your product performs right now, especially with those first curious users. Maybe you track how many people sign up, how many come back, or how many tell their friends. The point is to get a clear snapshot of where things stand—before you start making changes.
Next, it’s time to tune the engine. Here’s where the real fun begins. You start running experiments—maybe you tweak a feature, adjust your pricing, or try a fresh marketing message. Each change is aimed at moving your most important numbers in the right direction. This gives you proof that, step by step, your business is getting stronger.
And finally, comes the tough decision: Should you pivot or persevere? You use your data to decide. If your key metrics are improving, maybe you’re ready to double down and scale up. But if things are stalling, sometimes it’s smarter to change direction—maybe by finding a new audience or trying a different approach.
Let’s make this real with an example. Imagine your team is launching a new subscription service. You start by tracking how many folks sign up for a free trial—that’s your baseline. Then, you experiment with different ways to welcome new users, hoping more of them will become paying subscribers. If, after a few rounds, the conversion rate is still low, it might be time to pivot. Maybe you look for a different group of customers, or rethink your pricing.
The secret sauce behind innovation accounting is focusing on actionable metrics—numbers that actually reflect what your customers are doing and whether your business is growing. It’s not about chasing vanity metrics, like total downloads, that look good but don’t truly matter. Instead, you want to know how many people are consistently using your product and coming back every week.
To keep everyone in the loop, simple dashboards or spreadsheets can help you see how things are changing over time. The trick is to look for trends and patterns, not just isolated numbers. This way, you can spot whether your efforts are paying off, or if it’s time to try something new.
When teams embrace innovation accounting, they create a culture where everyone can see how decisions get made—and what impact they have. It cuts down on guesswork and makes sure your time, energy, and resources are going where they’ll make the biggest difference.
So, if you want to build something that lasts, don’t just measure what’s easy. Measure what really matters, and let those signposts guide you toward sustainable growth.
